label: praemorse
definition: A truncated quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's ending abruptly in an irregular, jagged edge, as if bitten or broken off.
reason: Rhizomes, leaf and petal apices 'praemorse' are truncate with a ragged edge; PATO:0000936 truncated lacks the jagged end and PATO:0001368 erose is a margin, not an end.
Only used of anther thecae, where 'distinct' means not united (rule C177 to free); 'sub-' is the approximate-value pattern, as for suborbicular.

label: tripinnatifid
definition: A pinnatifid quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's lobes being themselves pinnatifid and their lobes pinnatifid in turn, so that the bearer is three times pinnately incised.
reason: A frequent fern and Apiaceae leaf division with no term; follows FLOPO:0991159 tripinnate as the pinnatifid counterpart.

label: horn-shaped
definition: A convex 3-D shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being elongated, tapering to a point and usually curved, like an animal horn.
reason: The whole structure (spur, calyptra, appendage) has the shape of a horn; FLOPO:0991029 horned is bearing horn-like projections and PATO:0002161 bicornuate is having two horns.
Negation of the existing class secund, used of inflorescences and flowers.

target: docs/odp/01-approximate-value.md (approximately scapose; 'scapose' has no class yet)
reason: 'Nearly scapose' is the approximate-value pattern on 'scapose', which needs a class first; 'peduncle present' would not do, because every inflorescence has a peduncle.
config/botanical_colour_synonyms.tsv maps rust, rusty, ferruginous and rouille to the colour class orange; PATO:0070059 rusty is oxidation, not colour.

label: semiovate
definition: A 2-D shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's outline being one half of an ovate figure divided lengthwise, with one side nearly straight and the other curved.
reason: An asymmetric outline of side lobes, stipules and sepals; it is not ovate (FLOPO:0991024), much as PATO:0002232 semicircular is not circular.

target: new: merosity (number of parts per floral whorl)
reason: A count of parts in each whorl; docs/odp/03-count-of-parts.md leaves '-merous' unsplit because it names no single part, so a merosity pattern is needed rather than a term per number.
Lobes, sepals and leaves not overlapping each other negates the like-parts class imbricate; PATO:0002488 overlapping is relational and needs a second part.
Same as 'rust colored': rust and ferruginous map to the colour class orange in the colour lexicon.

label: induplicate
definition: A folded quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's margins or segments being folded inwards or upwards, towards the axis or the adaxial side.
reason: Used of petals in bud (induplicate-valvate) and of palm leaf segments (V-shaped in section); sibling of FLOPO:0991123 conduplicate and PATO:0104365 plicate.
Headlike inflorescences are compact head-like clusters; 'head-like' is already a synonym of capitate.
Margins not ciliate negates ciliated, which the flora pipeline already uses for 'ciliate' (config/flora_union_pairs.tsv).
Nervose means with evident veins, the same as the rules for 'veined' (C211) and 'nerved' (C212).
Long-ovate is ovate but narrower; 'long-' is a degree modifier of the outline, and the ovate value is safe to keep.
A branch or bud 'dominant' over the others is a comparison stated without its second term, like 'larger'.
Grasses forming a sod spread into a dense, low, continuous turf, which is the mat-forming habit; it is not tufted (caespitose).

label: mamillose
definition: A texture quality inhering in a bearer, usually a cell or cellular surface, by virtue of the bearer's outer wall bulging outwards as a whole into a nipple-like swelling into which the cell lumen extends.
reason: In bryophytes mamillose (the whole cell wall bulges) is kept apart from papillose (a solid wall outgrowth, FLOPO:0991059); the floras use both side by side.

label: monolete
definition: A structural quality inhering in a spore by virtue of the spore's having a single straight scar (laesura) on its proximal face.
reason: A standard fern spore character with no term; trilete would be its sibling.
Pits arranged in a network separated by ridges are the honeycomb surface of alveolate; a single existing value is better than a two-value compound.
A midrib or vein raised above the surface stands out from it: the counterpart of 'impressed' to sunken (C216); PATO:0001369 raised is for bacterial colonies.
Band-shaped leaves, petals and filaments are long, narrow and flat, i.e. strap-shaped; PATO:0040014 band shaped is a strip encircling an object.
Flowers in glomerules are in dense clusters: PATO:0001629 aggregated (synonym clustered); capitate requires a head on a shortened axis.
Same as 'not ciliate', including French 'non cilié' and 'non ciliolé'.
PATO:0002212 slender has gracile as a RELATED synonym; used of stems, pedicels and whole plants.
A comparison stated without its second term (thicker-walled than which cells), like 'narrower' and 'shorter'.

label: petiole-like
definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer, usually the base of a leaf blade, by virtue of the bearer's being narrowed into a stalk resembling a petiole.
reason: Leaves tapering into a petiole-like base are common in sessile leaves; sibling of FLOPO:0991200 bract-like and PATO:0002457 leaf-like.
Laxly flowered inflorescences have loosely arranged flowers: the adverb of 'lax', which maps to loose (C169).
Lateral veins connected near the margin rejoin one another, which is anastomosing; the other uses (pinnules joined by a wing, stamens) are relations without a second term and stay unmapped.
